title: British American Tobacco (BTI) Deep Dive Analysis
summary: A defensive fiscal view accompanies tobacco value.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: Hiring slowed after the reopening burst and full payroll recovery took until July 2022. Stagnation overstates continued positive hiring, but the stated fast-partial-then-slow shape is supported.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: July 2020 employment situation
evidence.finding: Payrolls rose 1.8 m in July after 4.8 m in June and 2.7 m in May; unemployment fell to 10.2%. Permanent job losers were approximately unchanged at 2.9 m in July; temporary layoffs fell 1.3 m.

evidence.title: July 2022 Employment Situation release
evidence.finding: The release reported payroll employment and unemployment rate had returned to February 2020 levels in July 2022. This is a publication-vintage recovery date, not a claim about subsequently revised payroll history.

claims.reason: Fraud and administrative problems existed, but PUA covered more than a narrow BLS self-employed category and claim weeks were not unique recipients. The 30 m-person interpretation and fraud inference from mismatched denominators are unreliable.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: COVID-19 oversight report
evidence.finding: GAO found continued-claim totals counted weeks, not unique beneficiaries. DOL clarified this in December 2020; backlogs could produce several weeks per person in one report.

claims.reason: Large deficits and subsequent inflation support the broad warning; secular regime duration remains unspecified. Later quantitative tightening contradicts an assumption that ongoing deficits necessarily require continued Fed monetization.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: FY 2022 budget results
evidence.finding: FY 2021 deficit was $2.776 tn/12.3% GDP; FY 2022 $1.375 tn/5.5%. Receipts rose from $4.046 tn to $4.896 tn.

evidence.title: June 2022 Consumer Price Index
evidence.finding: June 2022 headline CPI rose 9.1% over twelve months.

evidence.title: July 2023 FOMC statement
evidence.finding: Federal funds target increased to 5.25-5.50%; Treasury/MBS holdings continued to decline. This was tightening rather than a permanent low-rate cap.

claims.reason: Q4 growth slowed from the exceptional Q3 rebound but stayed positive. Fiscal restraint is one possible cause among reopening arithmetic, infection waves and sector constraints.
claims.timing_assessment: Original horizon retained: until next stimulus
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: 2020 Q4 GDP second estimate
evidence.finding: Contemporary estimate: Q3 2020 real GDP +33.4% annualized, Q4 +4.1%. There was no renewed quarterly contraction in the second half of 2020.

claims.reason: Ten-year breakevens fell into September, then exceeded August levels by December 23, before the major package became law. Policy expectations may lead passage; the market is not a contemporaneous on/off fiscal switch.
claims.timing_assessment: Original horizon retained: until next fiscal package
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Ten-year inflation compensation sensitivity
evidence.finding: DGS 10 minus DFII 10: August 31, 2020 1.80%, September 14 1.65%, September 25 1.58%, December 23 1.97%. Breakeven includes inflation-risk and liquidity premia, not pure expected CPI.

evidence.title: CARES and Consolidated Appropriations Acts
evidence.finding: The subsequent broad relief act passed Congress December 21 and was signed December 27, 2020, after the election rather than during summer.

claims.reason: The author explicitly marks down her prior expectation; the major package was not signed until December 27. This is a useful forecast revision, not a new successful prediction of the earlier timing.

evidence.title: May 2020 personal income and outlays
evidence.finding: Personal income fell 4.2% in May after revised 10.8% growth in April. Declining recovery payments explained much of the decrease, partly offset by unemployment benefits. Spending rose 8.2%.

claims.reason: Higher premiums compensate for greater downside risk and do not establish positive risk-adjusted value. Willingness to own the underlying is a preference, not protection against a much lower clearing price.

claims.reason: American exercise is chosen by the holder; touching or crossing a strike does not automatically assign the seller before expiry. Assignment, exercise-by-exception and contrary instructions must be distinguished.

evidence.title: Options assignment FAQ
evidence.finding: American-style exercise is the holder's decision before expiration. At expiration, exercise-by-exception thresholds and contrary instructions apply; going in the money does not itself compel early assignment.

claims.reason: A strike range and indicative 6-8% premium are not an executed contract. Need exact expiry, strike, fill, collateral yield, assignments and subsequent shares before calculating return.

framework_lessons: Separate cash resilience from accounting impairment.
assessment: BTI eventually delivered favorable long-window returns, dividends and resumed buybacks, while its acquisition and sanctions risks materialized. The short-horizon fiscal outlook was less precise: breakevens recovered before new legislation. The option discussion contains an assignment error and does not disclose executed contract results.
